title: Impact of Mobile Phone Coverage on Market Prices

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
I will use Instrumental Variables (IV) regression with topographic suitability (z) as an instrument for mobile adoption (x). The key assumptions are: (1) Relevance: topographic suitability affects mobile adoption, (2) Exclusion restriction: topographic suitability only affects market prices through mobile adoption, and (3) Exogeneity: topographic suitability is uncorrelated with unobserved determinants of market prices.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(stargazer)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s76_data.csv")

# Display basic statistics
print("Data Summary:")
print(summary(data))

# Check instrument relevance (first stage)
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
print("\nFirst Stage Results:")
print(summary(first_stage))

# Test for weak instrument
f_stat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1]
print(paste("\nFirst Stage F-statistic:", round(f_stat, 3)))
print(paste("Weak instrument test (F > 10):", f_stat > 10))

# OLS estimation (for comparison)
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
print("\nOLS Results:")
print(summary(ols_model))

# IV estimation using 2SLS
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
print("\nIV Results:")
print(summary(iv_model))

# Extract key coefficient
iv_coefficient <- coef(iv_model)["x"]
print(paste("\nMain Result - IV Coefficient on Mobile Adoption:", round(iv_coefficient, 4)))

# Robustness checks
print("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===")

# 1. Test for endogeneity (Hausman test)
hausman_test <- summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE)
print("\nEndogeneity test p-value:")
print(hausman_test$diagnostics[1,4])

# 2. Overidentification test (if we had more instruments)
print("\nNote: Only one instrument available, so overidentification test not applicable")

# 3. Reduced form estimation
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
print("\nReduced Form Results:")
print(summary(reduced_form))

# 4. Check for outliers impact
print("\nRobustness to outliers:")
data_trimmed <- data[data$y > quantile(data$y, 0.05) & data$y < quantile(data$y, 0.95), ]
iv_robust <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data_trimmed)
iv_robust_coef <- coef(iv_robust)["x"]
print(paste("IV coefficient (5% trimmed):", round(iv_robust_coef, 4)))

# 5. Alternative specification without controls
iv_simple <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = data)
iv_simple_coef <- coef(iv_simple)["x"]
print(paste("IV coefficient (no controls):", round(iv_simple_coef, 4)))

# Summary table
print("\n=== SUMMARY OF RESULTS ===")
print(paste("OLS Coefficient:", round(coef(ols_model)["x"], 4)))
print(paste("IV Coefficient:", round(iv_coefficient, 4)))
print(paste("IV Standard Error:", round(summary(iv_model)$coefficients["x", "Std. Error"], 4)))
print(paste("IV t-statistic:", round(summary(iv_model)$coefficients["x", "t value"], 4)))
print(paste("IV p-value:", round(summary(iv_model)$coefficients["x", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4)))

# Effect size interpretation
print(paste("\nInterpretation: A 1-unit increase in mobile adoption leads to a", 
            round(iv_coefficient, 4), "unit change in market prices"))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a negative coefficient (around -0.3 to -0.7), indicating that mobile phone adoption reduces market prices. The economic mechanism is that better information flow through mobile phones reduces information asymmetries and search costs, leading to more competitive pricing and lower price dispersion. The IV estimate should be larger in absolute magnitude than OLS if there's positive selection bias (areas with naturally lower prices may be more likely to adopt mobile technology).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use topographic suitability as an instrument for mobile adoption.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased mobile adoption leads to a decrease in market prices.
